title: Personal best marathon time and longest training run, not anthropometry, predict performance in recreational 24-hour ultrarunners
authors: Knechtle B, Knechtle P, Rosemann T
journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
population: 63 male recreational ultrarunners in a 24-hour run (mean 146.1 km)
findings: Bivariate: longest training session r = 0.56, personal best marathon time r = -0.58, weekly km r = 0.31 with 24-h distance; anthropometric correlations weaker (r about -0.25 to -0.34).
Stepwise regression retained the longest training session and the marathon personal best.
Reported equation: distance (km) = 234.7 + 0.481 x longest training session (km) - 0.594 x marathon PB (min), r2 = 0.46.
limitations: Small, male-only, 24-hour format (not point-to-point); in-sample equation with no validation; r2 = 0.46 leaves most variance unexplained.
implications: Marathon PB and the longest training run are the best simple covariates for fixed-time ultra distance; use them as sanity-check inputs, not a production formula.
Do not code the published equation for anything beyond a plausibility check.
